pavagada_park.note: Cells with >=25% inside OSM solar polygons. Second row waives the 'built' exclusion/weight on those cells because WorldCover 2021 may label panels as built; this is applied to park cells only.

other_osm_solar.note: Cells holding OSM solar generators (points/small ways) outside the park cells; small n, mapping is patchy.

sensitivity.note: Ranking is by LCOE so tariff does not change the order, only which cells are viable (LCOE < tariff).

validation.pavagada_lcoe_percentiles_note: percentile = share of ranked cells with higher LCOE

vs_previous_run.note: measured manually in the run before this one (LCOE ranking before access road, heat derate, flood exclusion); the script cannot recompute it once the report is overwritten

a1_a2_link.precision_note: QA (reports/qa/pvg_solar.png, top 6 tiles by new-PV ha) looked at by eye: see qa_verdict. No ground truth beyond OSM footprints. construction_ha is dominated by seasonal/crop/burn change between two single dates and should NOT be read as built area; converted_2023_2025 (union) is therefore inflated, newpv_only variants are cleaner. Thresholds calibrated on OSM solar polygons vs nearby land: the rule fires on ~52-55% of polygon pixels and ~2-5% of surrounding land (which includes unmapped PV), so it undercounts PV area and picks up dark soil/rock/fallow as noise. A 10 m pixel cannot see panel rows; new_pv_ha is a lower-confidence estimate (seasonal dry-season pair, same month both years) and detections are leads, not a survey.
a1_a2_link.qa_verdict: Looked at top-6 tiles: 2 of 6 (tiles 805, 804: farmland -> grey panel blocks with access roads and a substation yard) are real new PV; the other 4 (1425, 1471, 1424, 1609) are dark rock/burn-scar/shadowed hillside false positives. Precision on top tiles ~33%; the rule cannot separate dark terrain from panels at 10 m. Hand-written after viewing the image; re-check it if thresholds change.

caveats: NASA POWER irradiance/wind is native ~0.5-1 deg: only 16 sample points, cell values are smooth interpolation, ridge-top wind NOT resolved (Global Wind Atlas would be the upgrade).
Slope-share and land-use share are multiplied as if independent.
Clusters chain adjacent 1 km cells, so cluster_mw can reach GW scale; block_mw_capped = min(cluster_mw, 500) is the realistic reporting size.
Substation distance is a straight-line proxy; no capacity, voltage-level or land-ownership data.
